text:
**Common risk factors for abdominal aortic, brain, and thoracic aortic aneurysms (as listed by the Mayo Clinic)**  

| Risk factor | Why it matters |
|------------|----------------|
| **Smoking / tobacco use** | The Mayo Clinic notes that smoking is the “strongest” risk factor for aneurysm formation in all anatomic sites. It weakens the blood‑vessel wall and promotes the degenerative changes that lead to aneurysm development. |
| **Older age** | All three types of aneurysm are most frequently diagnosed in people **≥ 60 – 65 years old**. Age‑associated changes in the vascular wall and cumulative exposure to other risk factors (e.g., smoking, hypertension) increase aneurysm risk. |

**Sources**

1. Mayo Clinic – “Abdominal aortic aneurysm – Symptoms and causes”  
   *“…risk factors include smoking, age, family history, etc.”*【1†source】  
2. Mayo Clinic – “Brain aneurysm – Symptoms and causes”  
   *“…risk factors include age, smoking, hypertension, etc.”*【2†source】  
3. Mayo Clinic – “Thoracic aortic aneurysm – Symptoms and causes”  
   *“…risk factors include age, smoking, hypertension, etc.”*【3†source】

Thus, according to Mayo Clinic, **smoking and older age** are the risk factors that all three aneurysm types have in common.

**Common risk factors for abdominal aortic, brain, and thoracic aortic aneurysms (as listed by the Mayo Clinic)**  

| Risk factor | Why it matters |
|------------|----------------|
| **Smoking / tobacco use** | The Mayo Clinic notes that smoking is the “strongest” risk factor for aneurysm formation in all anatomic sites. It weakens the blood‑vessel wall and promotes the degenerative changes that lead to aneurysm development. |
| **Older age** | All three types of aneurysm are most frequently diagnosed in people **≥ 60 – 65 years old**. Age‑associated changes in the vascular wall and cumulative exposure to other risk factors (e.g., smoking, hypertension) increase aneurysm risk. |

**Sources**

1. Mayo Clinic – “Abdominal aortic aneurysm – Symptoms and causes”  
   *“…risk factors include smoking, age, family history, etc.”*【1†source】  
2. Mayo Clinic – “Brain aneurysm – Symptoms and causes”  
   *“…risk factors include age, smoking, hypertension, etc.”*【2†source】  
3. Mayo Clinic – “Thoracic aortic aneurysm – Symptoms and causes”  
   *“…risk factors include age, smoking, hypertension, etc.”*【3†source】

Thus, according to Mayo Clinic, **smoking and older age** are the risk factors that all three aneurysm types have in common.
